Over 700 traditional hanok houses, the birthplace of bibimbap, and lively makgeolli alleys.

Overview

Jeonju (전주) is one of the essential stops in South Korea, located in the North Jeolla region. Over 700 traditional hanok houses, the birthplace of bibimbap, and lively makgeolli alleys.

With direct connections via KORAIL KTX & SRT High-Speed Rail, Jeonju rewards a stay of 1–2 days so you can balance major landmarks with neighborhood cafés, markets, and easy half-day excursions.

RegionNorth Jeolla
Best timeApr–Jun & Sep–Oct
Suggested stay1–2 days
Good forNorth Jeolla, Culture & Sightseeing, Food & Dining, Rail Hub

Neighbourhoods & areas

Jeonju Historic Center & Old Town

Walkable core with historic architecture, pedestrian squares, and landmarks (Jeonju Historic Center & Main Square).

Central Station & Transit Quarter

Convenient hub for KORAIL KTX & SRT High-Speed Rail arrivals, luggage lockers, and business hotels.

Market & Dining District

Evening bistros, traditional halls, and food stalls serving Traditional Jeonju House Specialty and Regional North Jeolla Market Dish.

Where to stay by budget

Budget

Well-connected hostels and guesthouses within a 10-minute walk of Jeonju's central station or metro lines.

Mid-range

Boutique 3-to-4-star hotels near the historic center and pedestrian promenade.

Luxury

Heritage 5-star grand hotels and design properties with concierge access and views.

Rough nightly ranges: hostels and capsule hotels often run a few thousand yen per person; business hotels commonly ₩8,000–₩20,000 per room; upscale hotels and ryokan can be far higher, especially in peak seasons. See our accommodation guide.

Getting there

Jeonju is served by KORAIL KTX & SRT High-Speed Rail and intercity express trains as well as regional airport transfers. Book high-speed legs 2–6 weeks ahead for early-bird fares.

Getting around

The historic core of Jeonju is best explored on foot, supplemented by contactless tap-to-pay metro, tram, or bus lines.

Day trips & side trips

Scenic Regional Excursion from Jeonju

30–60 minutes by regional train into the surrounding North Jeolla countryside and nearby historic towns.

Neighboring Heritage Town

Combine morning sightseeing with a long local lunch featuring Artisanal North Jeolla Pastry & Wine.

Best time to visit

Spring (April–June) and autumn (September–October) bring mild walking weather and harvest festivals to Jeonju. Summer offers long daylight hours, while winter brings festive markets and lower hotel rates.

Local tips

  • Start at Jeonju Historic Center & Main Square before 9:00 AM to beat day-trip tour groups.
  • Use contactless credit cards or mobile transit passes on Jeonju buses, trams, and metro gates.
  • Order Traditional Jeonju House Specialty at lunch for the best value set menus.
